🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Legendary Mexican cultural journalist, writer and historian Humberto Musacchio has died at 83.

Musacchio died on Wednesday night, November 4, 2026, at his home in the Condesa neighborhood of Mexico City, nine days after his 83rd birthday. His death was confirmed by his family and announced by editor Consuelo Sáizar de la Fuente, former director of the Fondo de Cultura Económica, and reported by El País, La Jornada, Excélsior and Aristegui Noticias. No cause of death has been publicly disclosed.

Born in Ciudad Obregón, Sonora, on October 26, 1943, Musacchio devoted 57 years to journalism. He began his career in 1969, led the cultural section of El Universal in 1971, and served as editor-in-chief of unomásuno. In 1984, he was part of the founding team of La Jornada, where he served as deputy director.

He went on to direct the cultural supplement Comala at El Financiero and the magazines Kiosco and Mira, and wrote for Reforma and Excélsior, where his column “La República de las Letras” ran from 2006 until his final column on October 26, 2026 — his 83rd birthday.

His most lasting work was the Diccionario Enciclopédico de México, published in four volumes in 1989 and later reissued as Milenios de México. His books also include Historia del periodismo cultural en México, ¿Quién es quién en la política mexicana? and México: 200 años de periodismo cultural. In March 2026, he received the Homenaje al Periodismo Cultural at the Feria Internacional del Libro de Coyoacán (FILCO).

He is survived by his wife, Duska, his son Aldo, and his daughters Marusia and Natalia.

Rest in Peace, Humberto Musacchio.

Sources: El País; La Jornada; Excélsior; Aristegui Noticias.
